title: Thermal behavior in FeCuCrCoNi high entropy alloy nanoparticles: an atomistic approach.

recollection.starting_material: FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy alloy nanoparticles (5–10 nm diameter)
recollection.intervention: atomistic molecular dynamics heating ramps from 300 K to 1800 K under NPT conditions
recollection.structure: initial equimolar fcc solid solution evolving to partially segregated core–shell morphology with Cu-rich shell and Fe/Cr/Co/Ni-rich core
recollection.mechanism: temperature-driven surface segregation of low-melting Cu and onset of local fcc→liquid transitions at particle surface, followed by inward diffusion and homogenization upon cooling
recollection.results: melting onset at ~900 K, complete liquefaction by ~1250 K, Cu surface concentration rising from 20 at.% to 60 at.%, recrystallized particle upon quench showing grain size ~3 nm; total latent heat ~0.5 kJ g⁻¹ (all values guessed)

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies atomistic MD heating from 300 K and an initially equimolar FCC alloy, but most specifics are incorrect. The paper found no persistent Cu-rich core–shell segregation or substantial liquid surface shell; instead, Fe and Cu showed early element-specific mobility, with melting involving diffusion from both surface and core. The quoted temperature range, particle sizes, melting temperatures, compositions, grain size, and latent heat are unsupported or inconsistent with the reported inverse-radius melting trend, c = -0.978, T0 = 2184 K, and Fe mobility increase near 1000 K.
